strengths: Clear and precise problem decomposition: the coupling observation between window-shift and KV-refresh is technically sound and well-articulated
Concrete complexity analysis (O(|N|×C) vs O(C^2)) grounds the contribution in theory
Quantified empirical claims (6.0% throughput, 3.3× cost reduction, 0.6pp quality delta) make the contribution falsifiable
weaknesses: The 6.0% throughput improvement is modest and the 3.3× cost reduction on refresh alone does not translate proportionally to end-to-end gains — the gap between these two numbers is unexplained
Evaluation is limited to a single benchmark (MBPP), which is insufficient to establish generality across dLLM tasks
The contribution is narrowly incremental: it decouples two hyperparameters of a single concurrent paper (Window-Diffusion, 2026), raising questions about standalone significance
No ablation is discussed in the introduction regarding how sensitive quality is to the choice of shift interval vs. refresh interval independently
The claim that 'naive refresh reduction degrades both quality and speed' is counterintuitive and requires explanation; the introduction asserts it without mechanism

ai_detection.reasoning: The introduction follows an extremely rigid template: one-paragraph context, one-paragraph prior work, one-paragraph gap, one-paragraph method, then a 4-bullet contribution list with parallel structure. Prose is uniformly clean with no hedging, no tangential observations, and no author voice. The formulaic bullet-point contribution section with numbered metrics is a strong AI-generation fingerprint.
